$comment: Project settings for the autonomous experiment workflow.
These rules are POLICY, not enforcement. An agent with Bash access runs as the same
user and could work around them. The only load-bearing safety layer is the external
guard started by tools/setup_guard.sh, which runs from a copy of its code outside this
repository. What these rules buy is that a mistake becomes a blocked call instead of a
silent charge, and that tampering becomes deliberate rather than accidental.

$comment_deny: Only the guard's own output files are hard-denied. The guard is a separate OS
process and does not go through Claude permissions, so denying these costs nothing
legitimate and removes any path to forging a budget snapshot or clearing the kill
$comment_ask: Everything else that must not drift is 'ask' rather than 'deny', including the
constitution and the campaign specs. 'deny' has no appeal, which would stop the human
maintaining their own tooling and rules — and a rulebook that cannot be edited goes
stale, which is its own failure. In an UNATTENDED session there is nobody to answer
the prompt, so an ask is effectively a block, which is where the protection matters.
And a change that does get approved is still caught at the next gate: the reviewer
verifies tools/checksums.sha256, which covers tools/, deploy/, scripts/, eval/, envs/,
configs/target/, the constitution AND every campaign spec. Detected-and-appealable
